title: Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture
main_claim: Every smooth projective contact Fano manifold of dimension 2n+1 >= 3 is contact-isomorphic to the adjoint variety of a simple Lie algebra. As a consequence, every positive quaternion-Kähler manifold of dimension 4m >= 8 is homothetic to a Wolf space. Proof outline: (1) Picard reduction via KPSW, Mori and Kobayashi–Ochiai. (2) Two free contact lines with complementary positive parts are smoothed into a very free conic with submersive two-point evaluation. (3) The invariant tensor (z-w)^2 ∂z⊗∂w gives two vector lifts that extend over the unmarked boundary of M_{0,0}(X,2). (4) Their common contact value descends to a symmetric section B of L⊠L on X×X. (5) The diagonal jets of B (quadratic term θ², cubic term forced by symmetry) make the map X→P(H^0(L)) an immersion, so H^0(L) generates first jets, contact Hamiltonians span T_X and the contact automorphisms act transitively. (6) The moment map identifies X with the adjoint variety, and LeBrun's twistor theorems give the quaternion-Kähler corollary.

issues.location: sections/lines.tex, Prop. lines:suitable-pair and the paragraph citing Kebekus2001 Thm 4.4 and Buczynski2010 Thm 3.1
issues.description: Key input not re-proved. At a general point the paper needs two facts it takes from the literature: the tangent directions of contact lines span P(F_x) (credited to Kebekus 2001, Theorem 4.4), and the variety of these directions Z_x is a smooth, possibly disconnected, Legendrian variety (Buczyński's corrected Theorem 3.1). The argument depends on the exact form of these statements, and given the history of errors in this area I could not check them against the cited papers.
issues.evidence: The cone-addition lemma and the complementary-Lagrangian conclusion need some pair of cone components with ω(a,b)≠0, which follows only from the spanning statement. The paper itself notes that only the corrected version of Buczyński's theorem is valid.

coverage:
I read every section in build/sections. Steps checked by hand:
- Cone-addition lemma: the Taylor-order argument (ω vanishes to third order on the diagonal of a Lagrangian cone, while the exact value has order 2k).
- Fixed-end obstruction: the Laurent constants are shared; W1=uA and W2=vD; linearized horizontality gives dα(a,b)=0.
- Very free splitting: O(2)+O(1)^{2n} from degree 2n+2.
- Boundary extension: θ∘de is divisible by τ^r because the coefficient lies in (u,v)∩R=(τ^r); the contracted-component order b_J=r; the pole table, including that both mixed products are cancelled since θde vanishes to order r on both A and J.
- Descent: the projection of W12 to the trivial quotient f^*T/P_f is constant on proper connected D; sheets are K-rational; the local branch model gives a component of degree ≥ e; purity and simple connectivity of X×X finish it.
- Jet criterion: the cubic term C=α·A follows from symmetry; the fixed-second-slot derivative; the immersion argument.
- Remaining parts: the moment-map identification (Borel fixed point, highest weight, H=Q) and the twistor/LeBrun deduction.
I did not independently verify the external citations (KPSW, Kebekus, Buczyński, Araujo–Kollár Thm 15, LeBrun Cor. 3.4).
